heading: INT. SLEEPER TRAIN - DINING CAR - NIGHT

units.text: INT. SLEEPER TRAIN - DINING CAR - NIGHT
White tablecloths, brass lamps swaying.
The train rocks through a moonless forest.
A single table is laid for six, but only five place settings are occupied.
LOUISE ARDEN (40s, pearls, composed) stirs her tea without drinking it.
Her husband ARTHUR (50s, crisp suit) cuts a steak into perfect squares.
DR. PELL (60s, round glasses, doctor's bag at his feet) reads the same page of a newspaper again and again.
Their daughter MINNIE (7, ribbon in hair) draws on a napkin.
A WAITER (20s, white jacket, stiff) hovers by the pantry door.
The sixth chair is empty.
The sixth place setting is untouched.
Another pot of tea, I think.
units.name: ARTHUR

units.text: Yes, sir.
units.name: WAITER

units.text: The Waiter doesn't move.
His eyes are on the empty chair.
The tea, please.
units.name: LOUISE

units.text: The Waiter jerks into motion.
He vanishes through the pantry door.
Dr. Pell turns a page that he hasn't read.
Mama, who is that man?
units.name: MINNIE

units.text: Louise sets down her spoon very gently.
What man, darling?
units.name: LOUISE

units.text: The one at the end. He's got no shoes.
units.name: MINNIE

units.text: Arthur's knife stops.
Dr. Pell folds his newspaper into precise quarters.
Minnie, eat your potatoes.
units.name: ARTHUR

units.text: At the far end of the car, the lamp over the sixth chair dims.
A PASSENGER (age impossible to tell, grey coat, wet hair, bare feet) is sitting there.
No one saw him arrive.
Good evening.
units.name: DR. PELL

units.text: Evening, Doctor.
units.name: PASSENGER

units.text: His voice is a dry rasp, like paper on stone.
He rests both hands on the tablecloth.
They leave damp prints.
I don't believe we've been introduced.
units.name: ARTHUR

units.text: I don't believe you'd want to be.
units.name: PASSENGER

units.text: Louise rises, smoothing her skirt, and walks to the sideboard.
She lifts a heavy silver coffee pot and keeps her back to the table.
You're traveling a long way?
units.name: LOUISE

units.text: Not as far as you.
units.name: PASSENGER

units.text: Minnie slides off her chair and walks toward him with her napkin drawing.
Arthur catches her wrist.
Minnie.
units.name: ARTHUR

units.text: He asked me to.
units.name: MINNIE

units.text: The Passenger takes the napkin.
On it, in crayon, a stick figure lies under a stick train.
Sexton. Enough.
units.name: DR. PELL

units.text: The Passenger smiles.
The dim lamp over him steadies, flaring warm.
So you do remember me, Doctor.
units.name: SEXTON

units.text: Dr. Pell stands, knocking his chair back.
Louise sets down the coffee pot with a hard click.
The Waiter comes through the pantry door with the tea tray and stops dead.
Sit down, everyone. The night is long, and the train does not stop until we've settled the account.
units.name: SEXTON

units.text: Nobody sits.
Nobody leaves.
The train rocks on.
